pr_title: Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins

validations.droid_claim:
[P2] Legacy `*-box-ordinal-group` is 1-based; `order` is 0-based

In the legacy `-webkit-box` / `-moz-box` flexbox syntax, `*-box-ordinal-group` is 1-based (default `1`), while modern `order` defaults to `0`. As written, `@include order(0)` would emit `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 0` which can misorder (or be invalid/ignored) on those legacy implementations. Consider emitting `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val + 1` (and same for `-moz-box-ordinal-group`) so the mixin preserves modern `order` semantics.
validations.impact: On legacy WebKit/Gecko browsers using -webkit-box/-moz-box layout, elements using @include order() will have incorrect ordering because box-ordinal-group is 1-based while the mixin passes the 0-based order value directly.
validations.reasoning: Verified in mixins.scss lines 123-128. The @mixin order($val) passes $val directly to both -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group. The legacy box-ordinal-group property is indeed 1-based (default 1, minimum valid value 1), while CSS order is 0-based (default 0). The PR uses @include order(2) in topic.scss:30 and @include order(3) in header.scss:39. While these won't crash, they produce semantically incorrect values for legacy browsers — order(0) would emit box-ordinal-group:0 which is invalid, and all values are off by one from their intended legacy equivalents.
